vendors.name: Alegion
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Healthcare, insurance, hospitality, retail, manufacturing computer-vision use cases
vendors.notes: Austin-based mid-size annotation vendor with a key delivery center in Kuala Lumpur; focuses on vertical-specific computer vision projects rather than general-purpose crowd scale.

vendors.name: Appen
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Enterprise NLP, search relevance, tech giants (long history with major search/social platforms)
vendors.compliance_notes: ISO 27001; publicly traded (ASX: APX) with formal data governance program
vendors.notes: One of the oldest and largest publicly traded AI data vendors, with a global crowd of over a million contributors across 235+ languages/dialects; has faced revenue declines as newer specialized vendors erode share.

vendors.name: Centific (formerly Pactera EDGE, incl. OneForma)
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Frontier AI/LLM labs, Microsoft/Nvidia partner ecosystem, enterprise AI data foundry
vendors.compliance_notes: Enterprise security program; SOC 2-aligned controls
vendors.notes: Rebrand of Pactera EDGE; operates the OneForma crowdsourcing app and markets itself as an 'AI data foundry' partnering directly with model labs like Nvidia; raised $60M in 2025 to scale.

vendors.name: CloudFactory
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Computer vision, document processing, insurance/fintech workflows
vendors.compliance_notes: ISO 27001, GDPR
vendors.notes: Global HQ in the Thames Valley (UK) with operational roots and major delivery centers in Nepal and Kenya; positions itself as a managed 'human-in-the-loop' workforce rather than a pure self-serve platform.

vendors.name: Cogito Tech
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Computer vision, generative AI/RLHF, autonomous systems
vendors.compliance_notes: ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR
vendors.notes: Positions itself as a managed-service data-development partner with delivery teams across Asia, North America, and Europe; publishes frequent industry benchmarking content on the data labeling market.

vendors.name: DataForce (by TransPerfect)
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Enterprise NLP, code-generation model training (vetted software engineers), multilingual AI
vendors.compliance_notes: Leverages TransPerfect's ISO 17100/ISO 9001 and enterprise security infrastructure
vendors.notes: Division of translation/localization giant TransPerfect, giving it an unusually deep bench of in-country linguistic and domain-vetted subject-matter experts versus generic crowd labor.

vendors.name: DataOcean AI (formerly Speechocean)
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Speech recognition/TTS across low-resource languages and dialects, enterprise voice AI
vendors.notes: Rebranded from Speechocean; one of the deepest catalogs of off-the-shelf speech datasets (1,100+ speech datasets, 1,300+ total), with strong multilingual/dialect coverage across 70+ countries of project delivery.

vendors.name: Datatang
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Autonomous driving (Sunnyvale, CA office serving Silicon Valley AV clients), off-the-shelf multimodal datasets
vendors.notes: Long-running Beijing-based AI data provider with 1,000+ enterprise customers and a large catalog of off-the-shelf licensable speech/image/video/text datasets in addition to custom collection.

vendors.name: Deepen AI
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Autonomous vehicles, robotics, ADAS scenario/safety databases
vendors.notes: Silicon Valley specialist in multi-sensor (camera, LiDAR, radar) annotation for AV/robotics; maintains the 'Safety Pool' scenario database (300,000+ test scenarios) used across the automated-driving industry.

vendors.name: Defined.ai (formerly DefinedCrowd)
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Conversational AI, voice assistants, enterprise LLM training
vendors.compliance_notes: GDPR-compliant ethical sourcing; contributor consent-based data licensing
vendors.notes: Rebranded from DefinedCrowd to reposition as an 'ethically sourced' AI data marketplace, with off-the-shelf licensable speech/text datasets alongside custom crowd collection.

vendors.name: Encord
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Physical AI/robotics, autonomous systems, medical imaging
vendors.compliance_notes: SOC 2, HIPAA-aligned controls, GDPR
vendors.notes: London-based data-development platform pivoting toward 'Physical AI' use cases, adding support for multimodal sensor streams, 3D point clouds, LiDAR, and telemetry alongside traditional image/video annotation.

vendors.name: Hive (thehive.ai)
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Content moderation, trust & safety, AI-generated content detection
vendors.notes: Runs its own Hive Work gig app to source labeled data at scale, feeding its own pretrained content-moderation/classification APIs — blending a data vendor and AI-model-company business model.

vendors.name: Hivemapper
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Mapping/geospatial AI, fleet and dashcam-based street-level imagery
vendors.notes: Distinctive Web3/token-incentivized model: a decentralized network of drivers with dashcams contributes street-level imagery for crypto rewards, building a continuously refreshed global map dataset (100M+ km covered) rather than relying on a dedicated survey fleet.

vendors.name: Humans in the Loop
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Responsible/ethical AI programs, computer vision for NGOs and enterprises
vendors.compliance_notes: Fair Work Policy; social-enterprise ethical labor practices
vendors.notes: Hybrid social enterprise (for-profit funding a nonprofit foundation) employing annotators from refugee and displaced communities across Bulgaria, Turkey, Malaysia, and the Middle East; a strong pick for ethical-sourcing-focused procurement.

vendors.name: iMerit
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Autonomous vehicles, healthcare/medical imaging, geospatial, generative AI
vendors.compliance_notes: ISO 27001:2013, SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, 21 CFR Part 11
vendors.notes: Impact-sourcing model drawing 80% of its 5,500+ person workforce from underserved communities in India, Africa, and the US; strong reputation in medical imaging and AV data given its compliance certifications.

vendors.name: Innodata
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Frontier LLM labs, enterprise generative AI data preparation
vendors.compliance_notes: Public company (NASDAQ: INOD) with formal enterprise data governance/compliance program
vendors.notes: Publicly traded data-engineering company with roots predating the modern AI-data industry; its Digital Data Solutions segment has become a major supplier of training/evaluation data to frontier model labs, giving it audited public financials useful for vendor due diligence.

vendors.name: Kili Technology
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Enterprise ML teams in Europe and the US
vendors.compliance_notes: GDPR-native (EU-based)
vendors.notes: Paris-based annotation platform expanding into the US market; smaller headcount than US peers but differentiated by strong GDPR-native data handling for European enterprise clients.

vendors.name: Labelbox
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Enterprise AI data factories (Airbnb, John Deere, P&G cited as customers), generative AI/RLHF
vendors.compliance_notes: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001:2022, HIPAA program, GDPR
vendors.notes: Positions itself as an 'AI data factory' platform pairing labeling software with a managed/orchestrated global workforce; broad enterprise customer base spanning computer vision to LLM fine-tuning.

vendors.name: LXT (acquired Clickworker)
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Conversational AI, speech recognition, enterprise NLP across 1000+ language locales
vendors.compliance_notes: GDPR; formal data collection consent and privacy program
vendors.notes: Toronto-based AI training data provider that acquired long-running German crowdsourcing platform Clickworker (6M+ freelancers) in late 2024/early 2025, consolidating two major crowd platforms into one company.

vendors.name: Mercor
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Frontier LLM labs (OpenAI, Anthropic cited), expert-contributor RLHF data
vendors.notes: Started as an AI-driven recruiting marketplace before pivoting to supply vetted expert contributors (doctors, lawyers, engineers) for frontier-model training data; reached a reported $10B valuation within about two years — a talent-marketplace approach to sourcing high-skill annotators.

vendors.name: MOSTLY AI (powered by Syntho)
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Financial services, insurance (privacy-safe synthetic tabular data)
vendors.compliance_notes: GDPR-focused privacy-preserving synthetic data generation
vendors.notes: The original Vienna-founded MOSTLY AI entity ceased operations in March 2026; Amsterdam-based Syntho acquired the MOSTLY AI brand and SDK in June 2026 and continues the product line — a recent brand/ownership change worth flagging to procurement.

vendors.name: Objectways
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Generative AI, computer vision, content moderation
vendors.notes: Fast-growing US-based managed-workforce annotation vendor (targeting 3,000+ employees) that has scaled quickly on generative AI demand; less brand recognition than Scale/Appen but notable headcount growth trajectory worth monitoring.

vendors.name: Parallel Domain
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Autonomous vehicles, robotics simulation/testing
vendors.notes: Specializes in high-fidelity synthetic sensor data (camera, LiDAR) and 'digital twin' simulation (PD Replica) for AV and robotics edge-case testing where collecting enough real-world data is impractical or unsafe.

vendors.name: Prolific
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Academic behavioral research, RLHF/human-feedback data for AI labs
vendors.compliance_notes: GDPR (UK/EU based); participant vetting and identity verification
vendors.notes: Originated as an academic research-participant recruitment platform (30,000+ researchers) and expanded into supplying vetted human panels for AI training/feedback tasks, differentiated by strong participant-quality controls versus generic crowd marketplaces.

vendors.name: Sama (Samasource)
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Computer vision, autonomous vehicles, generative AI safety (RLHF), Fortune 2000 (Walmart, Nvidia, GM, Google cited as past clients)
vendors.compliance_notes: GDPR; Fair Trade-certified ethical AI workforce practices
vendors.notes: Began as a nonprofit-linked impact-sourcing model employing workers in East Africa; well known both for computer-vision annotation and for controversy over content-moderation working conditions.

vendors.name: Scale AI
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Autonomous vehicles, government/defense, generative AI/LLM evaluation
vendors.compliance_notes: SOC 2 Type 2
vendors.notes: The category-defining large-scale data vendor across AV, generative AI, and government; received a $14B strategic investment from Meta in 2025, prompting some AI labs to diversify away from it over neutrality/conflict-of-interest concerns worth flagging in vendor risk review.

vendors.name: Shaip (part of Ubiquity Global Services)
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Healthcare AI, clinical NLP, conversational AI
vendors.compliance_notes: HIPAA-compliant, ISO 27001
vendors.notes: Roots in medical transcription give it particular strength in HIPAA-compliant healthcare data licensing/annotation; acquired by Ubiquity Global Services in Feb 2026 but continues operating under the Shaip brand.

vendors.name: SuperAnnotate
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Computer vision, generative AI/LLM data curation for enterprise
vendors.compliance_notes: SOC 2
vendors.notes: Series B annotation/data-curation platform combining self-serve tooling with an orchestrated labeling workforce and QA automation; grown substantially in headcount over 2024-2026.

vendors.name: Surge AI
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Frontier LLM labs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, Microsoft cited), RLHF and RL-environment data
vendors.notes: Bootstrapped and highly profitable (reported ~$1.4B 2025 revenue) despite a lean ~130-person FTE core; curated, higher-skill contributor pool for RLHF rather than a large undifferentiated crowd.

vendors.name: Synthesis AI
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Computer vision (face/human-centric models), biometrics, AR/VR
vendors.compliance_notes: Privacy-by-design synthetic identities (avoids real biometric PII)
vendors.notes: Focused specifically on photorealistic synthetic humans/faces for computer vision training, sidestepping the consent and privacy issues of real biometric data collection.

vendors.name: TELUS Digital AI Data Solutions (formerly Lionbridge AI)
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Search/social platform relevance, autonomous vehicles (via acquired Playment), enterprise AI
vendors.compliance_notes: SOC 2, GDPR-aligned data governance program
vendors.employee_size_range: 50000+ (TELUS Digital overall; AI unit is a division)
vendors.notes: TELUS International acquired Lionbridge's AI division in 2021 and later acquired autonomous-vehicle data annotator Playment; operates a proprietary crowd platform (~1M annotators) covering 500+ languages/dialects.

vendors.name: Toloka AI
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: LLM fine-tuning/RLHF, generative AI evaluation
vendors.compliance_notes: GDPR-aligned; part of Nasdaq-listed Nebius Group
vendors.notes: Originated inside Yandex as an internal crowdsourcing tool before spinning out; now a standalone unit of Nebius Group focused heavily on RLHF and LLM evaluation data at scale.

vendors.name: V7 (V7 Labs)
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Computer vision, medical imaging AI, document automation
vendors.notes: Originated as computer-vision startup Aipoly before rebranding; known for auto-annotation/active-learning tooling (Darwin platform) rather than providing its own labor force — appeals to teams wanting self-serve over managed services.

vendors.name: Way With Words
vendors.notable_clients_or_industries: Speech recognition training data, transcription/captioning for enterprise and media
vendors.compliance_notes: GDPR-aligned; confidentiality/NDA-driven workflows for sensitive audio
vendors.notes: Niche specialist originally built around human transcription and captioning, extended into bespoke speech-data collection for ASR training; registered entities in the UK, Australia, and South Africa.
